title: A lesson target only the text supplies
statement: Choose a lesson's target idea so that it can't be stated correctly without reading the text, since a takeaway every learner already knows makes the whole lesson blind-solvable.
detail: Research before authoring a lesson on a famous episode found that the usual takeaway is the best-known fact about its hero and the answer a published class magazine prints in its own key, so a child who never read the passage would produce it (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/research/g4-u1-l2-the-cyclops.md`, lines 446-450). The brief argued that such a lesson fails the course's rule that a question must not be answerable without the text at the level of the lesson rather than the item, and that its evidence hunt degenerates, since a hunt with nothing genuinely rejected is a reveal (lines 448-456; `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/rules/questions-and-assessment.md`, line 41). The lesson plan rejected that takeaway for this reason (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/content/lesson-plans/g4-u1-l2.json`, line 60).
against: The brief marks the section as argument: "Yes. This section is my argument, not a finding." (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/research/g4-u1-l2-the-cyclops.md`, line 442).

evidence.quote: A SPINE lesson whose target concept can be stated correctly without reading fails R-Q-3 at the level of the lesson rather than the item.
R-PED-5 forbids modelling hard thinking as if it were easy, and a hunt with nothing genuinely rejected is a reveal, which is why `validate-contracts.mjs` requires a rejection at all.
A question must not be answerable without the text
it is the answer a child produces without reading anything, so a SPINE lesson built on it would fail R-Q-3 at the level of the lesson rather than the item.
Yes. This section is my argument, not a finding.
